title: Senior Software Engineer - Go SDK - Language Clients
locationText: Germany | Poland | Portugal | France | Spain | Italy | Israel | The Netherlands | Germany
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Integrations Ecosystem org builds the drivers, SDKs, connectors and BI integrations that make ClickHouse feel native in any stack. The Language Clients team maintains the official clients for Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, C++ and C#, plus the ODBC, JDBC and ADBC drivers. We're small, senior and remote across North America and EMEA.


THE ROLE

We're looking for a product-minded engineer to own ClickHouse's Go clients. You'll decide what the clients should do by talking to the developers who use them, reading the issues and the telemetry, and listening to the community. Then you'll build it, with deep Go expertise, and measure whether it worked. Your scope is the SDK and what builds on it: clickhouse-go and ch-go, and the collectors, pipelines, agents and tools that write millions of rows per second through your code.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Know who uses the clients and what they're trying to do. Define what good looks like (time to first query, error clarity, throughput, adoption by key integrations), measure it, and let that drive the roadmap.

 - Be the voice of ClickHouse for Go developers. Speak at GopherCon and Go meetups, and write the posts, tutorials and examples that developers and AI assistants find when they search for how to use ClickHouse from Go (SEO and GEO). Answer questions where the community asks them.

 - Own the Go clients and their ecosystem: clickhouse-go, ch-go, database/sql, releases and support. Evolve them without breaking the people who depend on them.

 - Keep the clients the fastest Go option for the fastest analytical database, and make sure the client is never the bottleneck. Performance is part of every release, not an afterthought: profile, change, measure again, catch regressions in CI, and publish the numbers.

 - Partner with the projects built on the clients, from the OpenTelemetry Collector to ClickHouse Grafana datasource and ClickPipes, and catch their regressions before they ship.

 - Review and co-maintain other clients, and take part in cross-client decisions on types, errors and protocol features.

 - Bring written proposals about where we invest next. You set direction rather than wait for it.

 - Make the clients enterprise-ready: TLS and mTLS, cloud authentication, safe credential handling, vulnerability response, a small dependency footprint, and the questions large Go shops ask before they adopt.

 - Shape the clients for agents as users: an API, docs and error messages an AI coding agent can use correctly on the first try.

 - Extend our AI development platform, with new workflows for maintaining the clients: consistency checks across languages, issue triage, release checks.


ABOUT YOU

 - Product-minded with a bias for action. You'd rather run an experiment and bring back data than wait for approval, you measure whether it worked, and you can explain what you chose not to build.

 - 5+ years in software, much of it on data-intensive systems: drivers, SDKs, ingestion, streaming, observability or analytics.

 - Deep Go expertise: the runtime and garbage collector, escape analysis, the memory model, pprof and the execution tracer. You reason about throughput and latency down to allocations and bytes on the wire, and you prove it with tests and benchmarks.

 - Strong Go concurrency instincts: context, goroutines and channels, bounded pools, backpressure, clean shutdown, and the leaks and races that come with each.

 - Beyond Go, productive in at least one more of our client languages (Python, JavaScript, Java, Rust, C++, C#). You'll review and co-own across clients.

 - You've built or substantially extended a Go module other engineers depend on. You understand semantic import versioning and treat breaking changes accordingly.

 - Strong grasp of database fundamentals: SQL, query execution and analytical workloads. Judgment about when to use database/sql and when to drop down to the protocol.

 - Enthusiastic about working in public. You've given talks or written technical content, or you're keen to, and you see it as part of the job rather than a distraction from it.

 - Thoughtful use of AI development tools, with the judgment to review what comes out.

 - Clear writing. Most coordination happens in design docs, PRs and RFCs.


NICE TO HAVE

 - ClickHouse, especially its type system and native format, or another columnar or OLAP engine.

 - Contributions to Go data or observability infrastructure: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Kafka clients, database drivers.

 - Building or maintaining a database/sql driver.

 - Apache Arrow or ADBC in Go.

 - Experience designing SDKs, docs or error messages with AI coding agents as the consumer.

 - Protocol or wire-format work on a database driver or network client.


LEARN MORE

 - clickhouse-go on GitHub https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go and ch-go on GitHub https://github.com/ClickHouse/ch-go

 - ClickHouse Go client documentation https://clickhouse.com/docs/integrations/language-clients/go

 - Chasing that 32 ms tail latency in ClickHouse https://clickhouse.com/blog/chasing-32ms-tail-latency-clickhouse


PERKS

 - Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

 - Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

 - Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

 - Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

 - A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

 - Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.


CULTURE - WE ALL SHAPE IT

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here https://clickhouse.com/company/careers. Check out our b

title: Research Engineering Manager, STEM
locationText: Brazil; Colombia, Huila, Colombia; Global - Remote | Global - Remote
description:
About Turing
Turing’s mission is to accelerate superintelligence to drive real economic progress. Headquartered in San Francisco, Turing works with frontier AI labs to generate high-quality datasets, reinforcement learning environments, and frontier research benchmarks that improve model capabilities in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and advanced STEM reasoning. In software engineering, Turing is the largest and longest-running data provider in the category. Turing also works with Fortune 500 enterprises across financial services, life sciences, healthcare, retail, automotive, and CPG to build and deploy end-to-end agentic AI systems inside mission-critical workflows. By operating on both sides, Turing closes the loop between frontier research and enterprise deployment, turning real-world deployment signals into better data, evaluations, and more capable models. Learn more at www.turing.com .
The Role
Turing builds large-scale datasets and reinforcement learning (RL) environments that power post-training for the world's leading AI labs and enterprises.
The STEM Horizontal team produces the high-signal coding and STEM data frontier labs train on. We're looking for a Research Engineering Manager to lead the research engineering behind its next layer: synthetic data that measurably improves models, and new benchmarks that measure what today's evals miss.
You'll lead a team of research engineers, work side by side with research scientists, and stay close enough to the code to review an eval harness line by line or prototype a generator yourself when the team needs it. You'll also build the team : hiring research engineers is a core part of this role, not a side task. Ideally you've been on the other side, at a frontier lab, and know what makes a lab trust a dataset or a benchmark result.
• Synthetic data that earns its place. Generation, verification, and filtering pipelines where every sample is checked, and where we can show which properties of the data drive downstream gains, not just how much of it we made.
• Benchmarks that stay meaningful. New evaluations for capabilities current benchmarks miss, built with calibrated difficulty, contamination controls, and statistics strong enough that a lab can make a decision on the result.
Quality failures here are quiet. A subtle bug in a verifier doesn't crash anything; it ships thousands of wrong labels into someone's training run and costs weeks. If you want to build the team and the systems that catch that early, this is the seat.
What You'll Do
1. Build and Lead the Team
• Build the team: define the profiles you need, run hiring, and grow research engineers selected for research taste as much as engineering rigor.
• Run the team's operating rhythm: project selection, planning, experiment reviews, design docs, and clear ownership.
• Coach engineers on experimental design, code quality, and presenting results; give direct, regular feedback and run fair performance cycles.
• Define the standards the team works to: eval methodology, data quality bars, and reproducibility — every dataset and result can be regenerated from a commit, a config, and a seed.
2. Partner with Research Scientists
• Turn hypotheses into experiment plans together: what we're testing, the baseline, the ablations, and the result that would change our minds.
• Set the agenda with research scientists. You're expected to bring your own hypotheses, not only implement theirs.
• Take research prototypes to production scale without losing the scientific intent.
3. Build Synthetic Data Systems at Scale
• Own synthetic data pipelines that generate, verify, filter, deduplicate, and version data, combining programmatic generators, LLM-based generation, automated verifiers, and targeted expert review.
• Judge data by its effect on models : ablations and fine-tuning or RL experiments that show which attributes (difficulty, diversity, correctness, coverage) drive gains.
• Build quality systems that hold up at volume: gold sets, LLM-judge calibration against expert labels, sampling audits, and agreement metrics.
4. Create New Benchmarks and Evaluations
• Find where frontier models fail and where existing benchmarks have saturated, and design evaluations that measure what's missing .
• Own benchmark methodology end to end: task taxonomy, difficulty calibration, graders and verifiers, contamination controls, held-out splits, and confidence intervals.
• Ship eval harnesses , including agentic and sandboxed-execution evals, that are deterministic, reproducible, and trusted by internal teams and partner labs.
• Make the call on whether a result holds up: partner labs and internal teams act on your sign-off.
• Publish benchmarks, datasets, and findings with our research scientists at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR.
5. Stay Hands-On and Work with Frontier Labs
• Write code every week on the hardest, highest-leverage parts: core verifier logic, eval statistics, the pipeline component everything else depends on. Expect a third or more of your time on direct technical work.
• Be the person the team brings its hardest debugging and methodology questions to: why a judge disagrees with experts, why an eval number moved, whether a gain is real or noise.
• Act as a technical counterpart to researchers at frontier AI labs: scope requests, set acceptance criteria, and explain results and trade-offs plainly.
• Partner with Strategic Project Leads, delivery, and engineering teams so research advances land in client work and in the platforms the team builds.
Sample Projects
• Identify a capability gap, design and ship a benchmark for it, and see it adopted by partner labs.
• Stand up a synthetic data pipeline for long-horizon coding tasks with execution-based verifiers, and run the ablations that show which task properties drive RL gains.
• Calibrate an LLM-judge grading system against expert labels, map where it fails, and decide where humans stay in the loop.
• Design the experiment

title: Founding Engineer
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Join an early-stage AI company building software and AI-powered services for renewable energy project diligence. You'll own the product experience and platform, working directly with customers and expert reviewers to deliver reliable, source-grounded analysis that helps projects move forward.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Talk with customers and translate their needs into product features.

 - Design, build, and ship full-stack product experiences used by customers, analysts, and expert reviewers.

 - Develop and operate AI-native workflows for assembling document sets, extracting and citing terms, drafting diligence materials, and preparing investment memos.

 - Measure shipped work with clear metrics and run experiments to improve product performance.

 - Build systems that trace claims to source documents and route unsupported questions to expert review rather than guessing.

 - Protect sensitive customer information through data isolation, least-privilege access, and auditability.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - At least 2 years of experience, including startup experience as a founding engineer or an early team member.

 - Full-stack engineering experience across frontend and backend, with a record of shipping products end to end and measuring results.

 - Demonstrated experience building generative AI products, such as RAG, function-calling, agent architectures, or LLM-powered workflows.

 - Experience with document processing, retrieval, or information extraction systems is useful.

 - Familiarity with Rails, React, Postgres, or Elasticsearch is a plus.

 - Background in fintech, legaltech, proptech, infrastructure, or energy is valued, as is experience securing sensitive data.

 - Ability to work in US time zones, including PT, MT, CT, or ET.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary: $130,000 to $150,000 annually. Meaningful equity at seed stage and a 401(k) with a match are offered. Visa sponsorship is not available.


LOCATION

Remote. Primary location: Canada.

description:
About Us
At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.
At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.
Locations-
• Austin
• NYC
• London
• Lisbon
About the Team and Role
The Developer Productivity team builds internal tools and platforms that improve the velocity and developer experience of Cloudflare's engineering teams. We own developer productivity (code commit to production), developer insights and ADLC metrics, developer infrastructure (CI/CD, build systems), AI-assisted development, and Cloudflare-on-Cloudflare dogfooding.
This team is responsible for AI-assisted development across all of Cloudflare engineering. Adoption has grown 4–6x in the last year. It's a small team, so you'll have a big surface area and real ownership from day one.
As a Software Engineer, you will help build and operate internal platforms that help Cloudflare engineers develop, deploy, and run software safely and efficiently. You’ll work across developer tooling, CI/CD, GitOps, and AI-assisted development, including MCP servers, agents, evals, and context engineering.
You’ll also help govern and enforce Cloudflare’s Engineering Codex by turning engineering standards into automated guardrails, paved paths, and actionable feedback.
What You’ll Do
- Build developer productivity tools, MCP servers, and AI agents.
- Automate Engineering Codex controls through CI/CD checks, templates, and policy-as-code.
- Monitor Codex adoption, improve controls, and support remediation and exception workflows.
- Improve GitOps, developer experience, platform security, and reliability.
- Partner with product teams on architecture and platform adoption.
- Respond to and prevent incidents affecting internal platforms.
What We’re Looking For
- Experience with TypeScript, Go, or Bash.
- Strong debugging and source-control skills.
- Experience with CI/CD, GitOps, or developer platforms.
- Ability to break down complex problems and evaluate trade-offs.
- Clear communication and a strong focus on developer experience.
Bonus Points
- Experience with AI agents, MCP, evals, or LLM-based tooling.
- Experience with policy-as-code or compliance automation.
- Background in platform engineering or developer productivity.
- Experience operating distributed or Kubernetes-based systems.
What Makes Cloudflare Special?
We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.
Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.
Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.
1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.
Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!
Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs. More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process.
This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.
Cloudflare is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all people and place great value in both diversity and inclusiveness. All qualified applicant

title: Curriculum Manager - AI Engineering
locationText: Belgium; Portugal; United Kingdom; United States | Belgium | Remote | United Kingdom | United States
description:
About DataCamp
Data and AI skills are critical for thriving today, and DataCamp is the platform that empowers everyone to learn them. We help individuals and Fortune 1000 companies close the data and AI skills gap through world-class learning, hands-on training, and a global community of expert instructors.
In this role, you’ll combine AI skills, technical expertise, and passion for great didactic experiences to usher in the next generation of education .
About the role
This is an individual contributor role. You will collaborate with subject matter experts and leverage in-house-built cutting-edge AI tooling to scale high-quality course creation across AI engineering: building applications with large language models (LLMs), prompt and context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, and related topics such as evaluation, fine-tuning, guardrails, and LLMOps. Here's what your day-to-day will look like:
• Manage the entire content development lifecycle and deadlines.
• Source and recruit top-tier subject-matter experts as instructors.
• Collaborate with instructors to create engaging content.
• Consistently leverage AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and more to drive high-quality content production at scale.
• Design, review, and create content on LLM application development, prompt and context engineering, RAG and vector databases, agents and tool use, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring of AI systems, and related topics. You will review content from a learner perspective, ensuring it is technically accurate, reflects current AI engineering best practices in a fast-moving field, and is pedagogically effective.
• Continuously assess course performance using learner feedback and engagement data to drive improvements.
• Identify and prioritize existing curriculum gaps or new topics in DataCamp's AI engineering curriculum.
We’re excited about you because you have the following:
• A solid hands-on background building and shipping production AI applications as an AI engineer, machine learning engineer, or software engineer. Experience taking LLM-powered systems from prototype to production (e.g. evaluation, monitoring, cost and latency optimization) is a strong plus.
• Broad AI engineering fluency spanning LLM fundamentals, prompt and context engineering, RAG, agents, and evaluation, with additional depth in at least one area such as agentic systems, retrieval and search, fine-tuning, or LLMOps.
• A solid technical background in Python, with comfort working with LLM APIs (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic), open-source models and frameworks (e.g. Hugging Face, LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex), agentic systems, vector databases, Git, and the command line.
• Intuitive understanding of instructional design, with proven ability to structure and teach technical concepts clearly.
• Graduate degree (Master's or PhD) in Computer Science, AI, Machine Learning, or a related STEM field—or equivalent industry experience.
• Strong experience with agentic coding systems, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Replit. You consider yourself a sophisticated user of these tools.
Bonus if you have the following:
• A deep understanding of the DataCamp course format—you have an intuitive understanding of what makes a great DataCamp course.
• An existing network of potential subject matter experts who can become DataCamp instructors.
• An extensive track record of teaching AI engineering to technical audiences.
